The exactly bound transition:line:26 has guard=null in inspection_equivalent_facts and no SMT guard formula (only lines 22/23/24 are enumerated), and the S5 native-AST comparison backend ran to completion with verdict=false and counterexample {expected: 'front_distance > 10', observed: null}. This establishes the violation on exact facts. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal proposes that the opaque trigger front_distance_10 substitutes for the guard, but a discrete event trigger is a different, weaker carrier property than a comparable guard expression evaluated at runtime; the NL text itself distinguishes guard conditions from stimulus events, and no exact mapping or equivalence fact is supplied showing the trigger enforces the same runtime condition. This alternative is therefore defeated by the exact contract distinguishing guard from trigger and by the completed backend counterexample.

The exactly bound transition:line:26 has guard=null in inspection_equivalent_facts and no SMT guard formula (only lines 22/23/24 are enumerated), and the S5 native-AST comparison backend ran to completion with verdict=false and counterexample {expected: 'front_distance > 10', observed: null}. This establishes the violation on exact facts. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal proposes that the opaque trigger front_distance_10 substitutes for the guard, but a discrete event trigger is a different, weaker carrier property than a comparable guard expression evaluated at runtime; the NL text itself distinguishes guard conditions from stimulus events, and no exact mapping or equivalence fact is supplied showing the trigger enforces the same runtime condition. This alternative is therefore defeated by the exact contract distinguishing guard from trigger and by the completed backend counterexample.

(2) NL-CONTRACT-REF-013 (NL5-DERIVED power off consumer coverage) and REF-014 (HumanDriving->Final transition) are satisfied by transition:line:27.
